title: CSS
description: Learn how CSS styles web pages with colors, layouts, and responsive designs. Master selectors, the box model, Flexbox, and Grid to make beautiful sites.

roadmap.title: CSS Foundations
roadmap.blurb: Learn how to pick elements and give them colors and backgrounds!

roadmap.title: Spacing & Text
roadmap.blurb: Control space around boxes and make your text look great.

roadmap.title: Modern Layout
roadmap.blurb: Arrange things neatly with Flexbox and Grid, and make pages fit any screen.

topics.title: Selectors & Syntax
topics.description: Learn how to target HTML elements and write valid CSS rules.

questions.question: Which symbol is used to select an element by its id?
questions.hint: It is also used for anchors in links.
questions.explanation: An id selector starts with a hash, like #header, and matches the element whose id attribute equals that value.

questions.question: Which selector targets all elements that have class="box"?
questions.hint: Class selectors start with a dot.
questions.explanation: A class selector begins with a dot, so .box matches every element with class "box".

questions.question: What does the universal selector * match?
questions.hint: Think of the widest possible reach.
questions.explanation: The universal selector * matches every element on the page.

questions.question: What punctuation mark ends each CSS declaration inside a rule?
questions.hint: It separates one property:value from the next.
questions.explanation: Each declaration like color: red ends with a semicolon, so you can list multiple declarations in one rule.

questions.question: In the rule p { color: blue; }, what is the part 'p' called?
questions.hint: It chooses which elements get the styles.
questions.explanation: The selector (here, p) decides which HTML elements the declarations inside the curly braces apply to.

questions.question: Write a CSS rule that makes all <h1> elements have the color green.
questions.hint: Use the element name as the selector.
questions.explanation: An element (type) selector h1 targets every h1, and color: green sets the text color.

questions.question: Write a rule that gives every element with class "card" a 1px solid gray border.
questions.hint: Class selectors start with a dot.
questions.explanation: The class selector .card matches all cards, and the border shorthand sets width, style, and color at once.

questions.question: What does the selector "nav a" target?
questions.hint: A space between two selectors means descendant.
options: <a> elements that are descendants of a <nav>
An element that is both nav and a
questions.explanation: A space is the descendant combinator, so nav a matches any <a> nested inside a <nav>.

questions.question: Which selector applies the same style to both <h1> and <h2> at once?
questions.hint: A comma groups selectors.
questions.explanation: A comma creates a selector list, so h1, h2 applies the declarations to both element types.

questions.question: Which pseudo-class styles a link when the mouse pointer is over it?
questions.hint: Type the pseudo-class including its colon.
questions.explanation: The :hover pseudo-class applies styles while the user hovers the pointer over an element.

questions.question: Write a rule that selects <li> elements that are direct children of a <ul> and removes their bullets.
questions.hint: The > combinator means direct child; list-style-type removes bullets.
questions.explanation: ul > li matches only li elements directly inside a ul, and list-style-type: none hides the bullet markers.

questions.question: Two rules match the same paragraph: "p { color: red; }" and "#intro { color: blue; }". The paragraph has id="intro". What color is the text?
questions.hint: Compare the specificity of an id versus an element selector.
questions.explanation: An id selector has higher specificity than an element selector, so #intro wins and the text is blue.

questions.question: A button must always appear orange, even when other rules try to override it. Which keyword forces a declaration to win?
questions.hint: It is written after the value, like color: orange ____;
questions.explanation: Adding !important to a declaration makes it override normal cascade and specificity rules.

questions.question: A form has many inputs, but only the ones with type="text" should get a light yellow background. Write the rule using an attribute selector.
questions.hint: Use input[attribute="value"] syntax.
questions.explanation: The attribute selector input[type="text"] matches only text inputs, leaving other input types unchanged.

questions.question: Style the first <li> in every list differently by giving it bold text using a structural pseudo-class.
questions.hint: There is a pseudo-class for the first child of its type.
questions.explanation: li:first-child matches each li that is the first child of its parent, making only the first item bold.

topics.title: Colors & Backgrounds
topics.description: Learn how to set colors and create backgrounds for your elements.

questions.question: Which property sets the text color of an element?
questions.hint: It is a short, common word.
questions.explanation: The color property controls the foreground (text) color of an element.

questions.question: Which property sets the background color of an element?
questions.hint: It is a hyphenated property.
questions.explanation: background-color fills the element's background with a solid color.

questions.question: What does the hex color #FFFFFF represent?
questions.hint: All channels are at maximum.
questions.explanation: In hex, FF means full intensity for red, green, and blue, which combine to make white.

questions.question: In rgb(255, 0, 0), which color is produced?
questions.hint: Only the first channel is at full value.
questions.explanation: rgb sets red, green, and blue; here red is full (255) and the others are 0, so the result is red.

questions.question: What is the shortest hex code for black?
questions.hint: Three-digit hex shorthand uses repeated digits.
questions.explanation: #000 is shorthand for #000000, which means no red, green, or blue, producing black.

questions.question: Write a rule that gives the <body> a light blue background color.
questions.hint: Use a named color or hex value.
questions.explanation: background-color: lightblue fills the whole page background with the named color lightblue.

questions.question: Write a rule for the class "alert" with white text on a red background.
questions.hint: Set both color and background-color.
questions.explanation: color sets the text to white while background-color makes the box red, giving a clear alert style.

questions.question: What does the 4th value in rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5) control?
questions.hint: It ranges from 0 to 1.
questions.explanation: The alpha value in rgba sets opacity, where 0 is fully transparent and 1 is fully opaque.

questions.question: Which function creates a smooth color transition for a background?
questions.hint: It is set as a background image value.
questions.explanation: linear-gradient() generates an image of colors blending in a straight line, used as a background.

questions.question: Which property would you use to make an image fill an element's background?
questions.hint: It accepts a url() value.
questions.explanation: background-image: url(...) sets an image as the element's background.

questions.question: Write a rule for class "hero" that uses a top-to-bottom gradient from purple to pink.
questions.hint: linear-gradient(to bottom, color1, color2).
questions.explanation: linear-gradient(to bottom, ...) blends purple at the top into pink at the bottom as a background image.

questions.question: You set background-color: blue and opacity: 0.5 on a box. What happens?
questions.hint: Opacity affects the whole element, not just the background.
options: The entire box, including text, becomes 50% transparent
The text stays solid, only the box fades
questions.explanation: The opacity property makes the entire element and its contents semi-transparent, not just the background.

questions.question: You want a semi-transparent background but fully solid text. Which color format should the background use instead of opacity?
questions.hint: It includes an alpha channel.
questions.explanation: Using rgba (or hsla) for background-color affects only the background's transparency, leaving the text fully opaque.

questions.question: A card needs a background image that does not repeat and is centered and covers the whole area. Write the rules for class "banner".
questions.hint: Use background-image, background-repeat, background-position, and background-size.
questions.explanation: no-repeat stops tiling, center positions the image, and cover scales it to fill the element while keeping its aspect ratio.

questions.question: Define a reusable brand color as a custom property on :root, then use it for the color of class "brand".
questions.hint: Custom properties start with -- and are read with var().
questions.explanation: Defining --brand-color on :root makes it global, and var(--brand-color) reuses it so the color is easy to change in one place.

topics.title: Box Model & Spacing
topics.description: Understand how margin, border, padding, and content build every box.

questions.question: Which property adds space INSIDE an element, between its content and border?
questions.hint: Think of padding inside a box.
questions.explanation: Padding is the space between an element's content and its border, inside the element.

questions.question: Which property adds space OUTSIDE an element, pushing other elements away?
questions.hint: It is the outermost layer of the box model.
questions.explanation: Margin is the space outside the border that separates an element from its neighbors.

questions.question: What are the four layers of the box model from inside to outside?
questions.hint: Content is in the middle.
questions.explanation: The box model goes content, then padding, then border, then margin from inside to outside.

questions.question: Which property draws a line around the edge of an element's box?
questions.hint: It sits between padding and margin.
questions.explanation: The border property draws a line around the padding and content of an element.

questions.question: Write a rule for class "box" that adds 20px of padding on all sides.
questions.hint: One value applies to all sides.
questions.explanation: A single padding value applies equally to the top, right, bottom, and left sides.

questions.question: Write a rule that centers a block element horizontally using auto margins, with a width of 600px.
questions.hint: Set width, then margin: 0 auto.
questions.explanation: With a fixed width, margin: 0 auto splits the leftover horizontal space evenly, centering the block.

questions.question: In margin: 10px 20px, what does the 20px apply to?
questions.hint: Two values mean vertical then horizontal.
questions.explanation: With two values, the first is top/bottom and the second is left/right, so 20px applies to left and right.

questions.question: By default (content-box), if a div has width: 200px and padding: 20px, what is its total rendered width?
questions.hint: Padding adds onto the width in content-box.
questions.explanation: With content-box, padding (20px on each side = 40px) is added to the 200px width, giving 240px total.

questions.question: Which box-sizing value makes width include padding and border?
questions.hint: It makes sizing more predictable.
questions.explanation: border-box includes padding and border within the declared width, so the element never grows beyond it.

questions.question: Which property rounds the corners of an element's box?
questions.hint: It is a border-related property.
questions.explanation: border-radius rounds the corners; larger values create more rounded or even circular shapes.

questions.question: Write a rule for class "avatar" that turns a 100px by 100px image into a circle.
questions.hint: border-radius: 50% on a square makes a circle.
questions.explanation: A 50% border-radius on a square element rounds all corners enough to form a perfect circle.

questions.question: Apply border-box sizing to every element using the universal selector.
questions.hint: Target * and set box-sizing.
questions.explanation: Setting box-sizing: border-box on all elements makes widths include padding and border, simplifying layouts.

questions.question: Two stacked block elements each have margin-bottom: 30px and margin-top: 20px. What is the gap between them?
questions.hint: Vertical margins collapse to the larger value.
questions.explanation: Adjacent vertical margins collapse, so the gap equals the larger margin (30px) rather than their sum.

questions.question: A designer wants a box that stays exactly 300px wide no matter how much padding is added. Which box-sizing value achieves this?
questions.hint: It keeps padding inside the declared width.
questions.explanation: With box-sizing: border-box, padding is included inside the 300px width, so the box never exceeds 300px.

questions.question: Create a button class with 10px top/bottom and 24px left/right padding, a 2px solid navy border, and 8px rounded corners.
questions.hint: Use the two-value padding shorthand.
questions.explanation: The padding shorthand sets vertical (10px) and horizontal (24px) spacing, while border and border-radius style the edges.

topics.title: Typography
topics.description: Style text with fonts, sizes, weights, spacing, and alignment.

questions.question: Which property changes the size of text?
questions.hint: It is about the font.
questions.explanation: font-size sets how large the text characters appear.

questions.question: Which property makes text bold?
questions.hint: It controls the thickness of letters.
questions.explanation: font-weight controls thickness; values like bold or 700 make text heavier.

questions.question: Which property makes text italic?
questions.hint: Style of the font.
questions.explanation: font-style: italic slants the text into an italic style.

questions.question: Which property horizontally aligns text to the center?
questions.hint: Set its value to center.
questions.explanation: text-align: center centers inline content like text within its block.

questions.question: Which property would you use to underline text?
questions.hint: It decorates the text.
questions.explanation: text-decoration: underline draws a line under text; it also controls overline and line-through.

questions.question:
Write a rule for

that sets the font size to 18px and centers the text.
questions.hint: Combine font-size and text-align.
questions.explanation: font-size makes the paragraph text 18px, and text-align: center horizontally centers it.

questions.question: Write a rule that removes the underline from all links (<a>).
questions.hint: text-decoration: none.
questions.explanation: text-decoration: none removes the default underline browsers add to links.

questions.question: What does font-family: Arial, sans-serif mean?
questions.hint: The second value is a fallback.
options: Use Arial; if unavailable, use any sans-serif font
questions.explanation: font-family lists fonts in order of preference; the browser uses Arial if present, otherwise a generic sans-serif.

questions.question: Which property controls the vertical space between lines of text?
questions.hint: It improves readability of paragraphs.
questions.explanation: line-height sets the height of each line, spacing wrapped lines further apart for readability.

questions.question: Which property changes text to all uppercase without editing the HTML?
questions.hint: It transforms the text case.
questions.explanation: text-transform: uppercase displays text in capitals while leaving the underlying HTML unchanged.

questions.question: Write a rule for class "heading" using a bold sans-serif font stack and 1.4 line-height.
questions.hint: font-weight, font-family, and line-height.
questions.explanation: The font-family provides a sans-serif stack, font-weight makes it bold, and a unitless line-height of 1.4 scales with the font size.

questions.question: You set font-size: 2em on a child whose parent has font-size: 16px. What is the child's font size?
questions.hint: em is relative to the parent's font size.
questions.explanation: em multiplies the parent's font size, so 2em of 16px equals 32px.

questions.question: Which length unit is always relative to the ROOT element's font size, ignoring parent sizes?
questions.hint: It starts with the letter r.
questions.explanation: rem is relative to the root (html) font size, so it is not affected by nested parent font sizes.

questions.question: Long words overflow a narrow box. Write a rule for class "note" that lets long words break to the next line.
questions.hint: overflow-wrap (or word-wrap) with break-word.
questions.explanation: overflow-wrap: break-word allows the browser to break long words so they wrap inside the box instead of overflowing.

questions.question: Truncate a single line of text with an ellipsis when it is too wide for class "title".
questions.hint: Combine white-space: nowrap, overflow: hidden, and text-overflow: ellipsis.
questions.explanation: nowrap keeps text on one line, overflow: hidden clips it, and text-overflow: ellipsis shows ... at the cut-off point.

topics.title: Flexbox
topics.description: Arrange items in flexible rows and columns with Flexbox.

questions.question: Which display value turns an element into a flex container?
questions.hint: It is a short word.
questions.explanation: display: flex makes an element a flex container and its children flex items.

questions.question: Which property sets the main axis direction of a flex container?
questions.hint: It controls row vs column.
questions.explanation: flex-direction sets whether items flow in a row or a column, defining the main axis.

questions.question: Which property aligns flex items along the MAIN axis?
questions.hint: It justifies content.
questions.explanation: justify-content distributes flex items along the main axis (e.g., center, space-between).

questions.question: Which property aligns flex items along the CROSS axis?
questions.hint: It aligns items perpendicular to the main axis.
questions.explanation: align-items controls alignment along the cross axis, such as centering items vertically in a row.

questions.question: Which property adds space between flex items without using margins?
questions.hint: It is a single short word.
questions.explanation: The gap property adds consistent spacing between flex items.

questions.question: Write a rule for class "row" that becomes a flex container laying items in a row.
questions.hint: display: flex defaults to row.
questions.explanation: display: flex creates the flex container, and flex-direction: row arranges items horizontally.

questions.question: Write a rule for class "center" that centers its children both horizontally and vertically.
questions.hint: Use justify-content and align-items both set to center.
questions.explanation: In a flex container, justify-content: center centers on the main axis and align-items: center on the cross axis.

questions.question: What does justify-content: space-between do?
questions.hint: Where does the empty space go?
options: Adds equal space around every item
Puts equal space between items, none at the ends
questions.explanation: space-between places the first and last items at the edges and distributes remaining space evenly between items.

questions.question: Which property lets flex items move to a new line when there is not enough room?
questions.hint: It wraps the items.
questions.explanation: flex-wrap: wrap allows items to flow onto multiple lines instead of overflowing the container.

questions.question: Which flex-item property tells an item how much of the leftover space to take, relative to siblings?
questions.hint: It is a number like 1 or 2.
questions.explanation: flex-grow sets how much an item expands to fill free space compared to its siblings.

questions.question: Write a rule so that items in class "nav" sit at opposite ends with vertical centering.
questions.hint: space-between on main axis, center on cross axis.
questions.explanation: space-between pushes items to the two ends, and align-items: center vertically centers them, a common navbar pattern.

questions.question: The shorthand flex: 1 is equivalent to which set of values?
questions.hint: It expands flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis.
questions.explanation: flex: 1 expands to flex-grow: 1, flex-shrink: 1, and flex-basis: 0%, letting items share space equally from a zero base.

questions.question: In a flex row, which single property on one item can push it to the far right while others stay left?
questions.hint: Use an auto value on a spacing property.
questions.explanation: Setting margin-left: auto on an item absorbs all free space to its left, pushing that item to the right edge.

questions.question: Build a responsive card grid using Flexbox: container class "cards" wraps items, has a 16px gap, and each ".cards > div" grows but is at least 200px wide.
questions.hint: Use flex-wrap and gap on the container, and the flex shorthand with a basis on items.
questions.explanation: flex-wrap and gap arrange wrapping rows, while flex: 1 1 200px lets each card grow and shrink from a 200px basis for a responsive layout.

questions.question: A sticky footer layout: make class "page" a vertical flex container that fills the viewport height, with the main content area growing to fill space.
questions.hint: Column direction, min-height: 100vh, and flex-grow on the main area.
questions.explanation: A column flex container at 100vh with flex-grow: 1 on main pushes the footer to the bottom even when content is short.

topics.title: Grid & Responsive Design
topics.description: Create two-dimensional layouts with Grid and adapt them to any screen.

questions.question: Which display value creates a grid container?
questions.hint: It is named after the layout.
questions.explanation: display: grid turns an element into a grid container with rows and columns.

questions.question: Which property defines the columns of a grid?
questions.hint: It names the template tracks for columns.
questions.explanation: grid-template-columns lists the size of each column track in the grid.

questions.question: What does the fr unit represent in Grid?
questions.hint: It is short for fraction.
options: A fraction of the available space
questions.explanation: The fr unit represents a fraction of the leftover free space in the grid container.

questions.question: Which property adds space between both grid rows and columns at once?
questions.hint: Same short word used in Flexbox.
questions.explanation: The gap property sets spacing between grid tracks for both rows and columns.

questions.question: Write a rule for class "grid" creating a 3-column grid where each column is equal width.
questions.hint: Use repeat() with the fr unit.
questions.explanation: repeat(3, 1fr) creates three equal columns, each taking one fraction of the available space.

questions.question: Write a rule for class "layout" with a 200px sidebar column and a flexible main column, plus a 20px gap.
questions.hint: Two values in grid-template-columns: a fixed one and 1fr.
questions.explanation: The first column is a fixed 200px sidebar and 1fr lets the main column fill the rest, with gap spacing them apart.

questions.question: What is a media query used for?
questions.hint: It checks conditions like screen width.
options: Applying styles only when conditions like screen width are met
questions.explanation: A media query applies CSS rules only when conditions such as viewport width are true, enabling responsive design.

questions.question: What does the meta viewport setting content="width=device-width" help with?
questions.hint: It relates to how mobile browsers size the page.
options: Making the page match the device's screen width
questions.explanation: width=device-width sets the layout viewport to the device width so responsive CSS works correctly on mobile.

questions.question: Which media feature checks the browser's width to apply mobile styles below 600px? Write the feature name.
questions.hint: It compares against a maximum width.
questions.explanation: A query like @media (max-width: 600px) applies styles when the viewport is 600px wide or narrower.

questions.question: Write a media query that makes class "grid" a single column on screens 600px wide or less.
questions.hint: Wrap the rule in @media (max-width: 600px).
questions.explanation: Inside the max-width media query, setting grid-template-columns to 1fr collapses the grid into a single column on small screens.

questions.question: Which property makes an image scale down to fit its container without overflowing? Write the declaration.
questions.hint: Limit the maximum width to 100%.
questions.explanation: max-width: 100% (often with height: auto) lets images shrink to fit their container while keeping aspect ratio.

questions.question: Which value lets a grid create as many equal columns as fit, wrapping automatically without media queries?
questions.hint: Combine repeat with auto-fit and minmax.
questions.explanation: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)) fits as many columns as possible at a minimum of 200px, making a responsive grid without media queries.

questions.question: Which property would you use on a grid item to make it span 2 columns?
questions.hint: It is about which column lines the item covers.
questions.explanation: grid-column (e.g., grid-column: span 2) makes a grid item stretch across two columns.

questions.question: Build a responsive auto-fitting card grid: class "cards" with columns at least 250px wide that wrap, and a 1rem gap.
questions.hint: Use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...)) and gap.
questions.explanation: auto-fit with minmax(250px, 1fr) creates as many 250px-or-wider columns as fit, wrapping responsively without media queries.

questions.question: Create a named-area page layout for class "page": a header on top, sidebar and content side by side, and a footer at the bottom.
questions.hint: Use grid-template-areas with quoted rows and grid-template-columns.
questions.explanation: grid-template-areas maps named regions to a visual layout, and each element claims its area with grid-area for a clear page structure.
